questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Get a written note from one real user or expert where possible.
Present to a review room: idea, task record, numbers, risks, decision.
Run a hygiene audit using your own checklist and note every gap.
Talk to 3 to 5 possible users or experts. Ask: what do you do now, what is hard, what would make you trust a new service?

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Licensing: many treatments need a licensed practitioner and a registered premises. Check what applies for each service and write down who told you.
Calculate break-even: rent, staff, products, laundry, energy against price and number of clients.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Peers list the three most serious gaps.
Run a hygiene audit using your own checklist and note every gap.
Write a hygiene routine: hand washing, cleaning between clients, laundry, waste, tool sterilising as local rules require.
Time every step and adjust the schedule.

questions.q: In "Short modules Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce in this course (listed at the end of each lesson).
Calculate break-even: rent, staff, products, laundry, energy against price and number of clients.
Licensing: many treatments need a licensed practitioner and a registered premises. Check what applies for each service and write down who told you.
Build a weekly schedule with treatment time, cleaning time and breaks.

questions.q: In "Continue and log Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Hygiene standards: clean hands, clean tools, clean surfaces, clean linen, and records of cleaning. Follow your local health authority's rules.
Take the 10-question check. Pass mark is 70% (draft).
Hygiene routine: wash hands, clean tools, fresh linen, wipe surfaces, record time.
Time every step and adjust the schedule.

questions.q: In "Review circle Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.
Finish the task and fix the biggest problem found in the circle.
Write a half-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Peers list the three most serious gaps.

questions.q: In "Finish and measure Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a 90-day next-step plan: what to do, where, how much, what to learn next. Pick a follow-on course from the catalogue.
Finish the task and fix the biggest problem found in the circle.
Present to a review room: idea, task record, numbers, risks, decision.
Fix them and re-audit.
